en: I also want to mention that Bun allows you
to access S3 files or files stored on
S3-compatible stores in another way. You can
use that Bun S3 client you saw throughout
the lecture, but you can also use the fetch
function and use an S3 URL like this.
This will not work in the browser or in
Node.js apps, but when using fetch in Bun
apps,
this will work. So that will require the
path of an object on that remote store and
it will then automatically use these env
vars here. So it will expect these names to
find out what the bucket name is and how to
authenticate with S3 or with the store
you're using. But it will do that
automatically if it sees that S3 URL
and it will then go ahead and fetch that
object.
You can also bring your own S3 configuration
as I'm doing it here. But again, this is not
needed. It would find that automatically.
I'm just I'm just doing it here for demo
purposes to show you how you could provide
your own config if you're using environment
variables that have a different name, for
example, so that differ from what is
expected. But that's then another way of
fetching a file from an S3 store. You can
use the BUN S3 client and that's what I
typically do, but you can also use the Fetch
API like this.
